newsitem.title: USA: USLIFE sees no layoffs from merger.
newsitem.headline: USLIFE sees no layoffs from merger.

text.p: USLIFE Corp chairman Gordon Crosby told investors he does not expect any positions to be eliminated as a result of the company's $1.8 billion merger with American General Corp.
"We don't anticipate any at the moment," Crosby told investors on a tense conference call.
Crosby also said there had been no decisions yet about senior management of the combined company.
He declined to project any potential cost savings from the merger or say where savings would come from if there would be no layoffs.
Instead, he referred listeners to the company's press release.
However, the press release does not discuss the cost savings expected from the deal.
The statement simply includes one comment from American General chief executive Robert Devlin on cost savings.

"Given the consolidation savings, we expect this transaction to be non-dilutive from its inception on a pro forma basis," Devlin said in the prepared statement that was released ahead of the conference call.
During the call, Crosby also told investors that the deal included a $48 million break up fee.
American General agreed to acquire USLIFE in a stock deal valued at $1.8 billion. Under the pact, USLIFE shareholders will receive $49 worth of American General stock for each USLIFE share.
